newsitem.title: CROATIA: LNG project in Croatia may be scrapped - report.
newsitem.headline: LNG project in Croatia may be scrapped - report.

text.p: A $1 billion project to build a terminal and pipeline for liquefied natural gas (LNG) in Croatia may be abandoned due to a lack of interest by central European states, local daily Vjesnik reported on Friday.
The Adria LNG project, launched in 1991, hinges on whether Italy's power firm ENEL joins it and invests in its further development, the well-informed newspaper said.
It quoted Herbert Stobl, director of a multinational consortium in charge of the project, as saying all plans "may be frozen" after years of development by consortium members.
These include a number of companies from former communist countries, the Croatian oil and gas firm INA with a 20 percent stake and France's Total SA.

But the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Hungary, which initially aimed to tap between 5.5 and 10 million cubic metres of LNG from the terminal on the island of Krk, are no longer interested in additional supplies to supplement their needs, Vjesnik said.
The cost of building the terminal is estimated at $700 million, with another $270 required for a northbound pipeline to central Europe.
To join the Adria LNG project, the Italian firm would have to build an underwater pipeline to bring gas across the Adriatic Sea.
